shared.text:
# Field Trial Summary: Fieldnote Clinic Pilot

From 1 September to 15 November, Fieldnote tested its offline notes app in Pune, Nagpur and Nashik. Nurses used shared tablets during home visits and synced their notes at clinic Wi-Fi. The pilot recorded 412 visits: 168 in Pune, 139 in Nagpur and 105 in Nashik.

## Results

The median sync time after returning to a clinic was 38 seconds. In Nashik, intermittent Wi-Fi sometimes delayed syncs by as much as four minutes. No notes were lost, and tablets lasted a full shift at all three clinics. Nurses gave the app an average rating of 4.3/5. The visit template was the most valued feature, reducing write-up time from about nine minutes to five. Photo upload was the least liked feature because it was slow and confusing.

Two incidents occurred. In Nagpur, two tablets editing the same visit offline created a duplicate patient record on 22 September; staff merged it manually that day. On 14 October, an expired sync-server certificate caused a three-hour outage. Neither incident harmed a patient.

## Spend and clinic feedback

The pilot used ₹18.5 lakh of its ₹22 lakh budget: ₹9 lakh for tablets, ₹4 lakh for training, ₹3.5 lakh for support and ₹2 lakh for the sync server. The remaining ₹3.5 lakh is reserved for the next phase.

Clinic leads requested simpler photo uploads, a warning when multiple tablets edit the same visit, and printed visit summaries for patients without phones. Nashik also asked to queue syncs until Wi-Fi is stable.

## Recommendation

The team recommends expanding to 10 clinics in March, contingent on fixing photo upload and adding the simultaneous-edit warning. It also recommends monitoring certificate expiry immediately. A second review is planned for June.
